facts.statement: Magyarosuchus is an extinct genus of thalattosuchian first described from fossils found in the Kisgerecse Marl Formation in Hungary.
facts.quote: Magyarosuchus is an extinct monotypic genus of metriorhynchoid thalattosuchian described for the first time from fossils discovered in the Kisgerecse Marl Formation in Hungary.

facts.statement: A fragmentary skeleton of Magyarosuchus was discovered in 1996.
facts.quote: It is known from a fragmentary skeleton discovered in 1996.

facts.statement: Magyarosuchus was a large thalattosuchian with a partial jaw that is deeper than those of close relatives like Pelagosaurus.
facts.quote: Magyarosuchus was a large thalattosuchian, the known partial jaw is deeper (taller) than other close relatives like Pelagosaurus

facts.statement: The holotype preserves many large, recurved teeth with a circular cross-section, non-serrated edges, and vertically aligned grooves.
facts.quote: Many isolated teeth are preserved in the holotype, these were large and recurved, possessing a circular cross-section and non-serrated edges, along vertically aligned grooves (fluting).

facts.statement: The femur and tibia of Magyarosuchus measure 36 cm and 21 cm in length, respectively.
facts.quote: its femur and tibia are 36 cm and 21 cm long respectively.

facts.statement: A posterior caudal vertebra in the holotype has a notably larger neural spine, which suggests the presence of a rudimentary vertical tail expansion similar to derived metriorhynchids.
facts.quote: the posterior-most one in the holotype; albeit incomplete, shows a noticeably larger neural spine than the ones before it. This might suggest the presence of a rudimentary vertical expansion (tail fluke) as is known in more derived metriorhynchid relatives.

facts.statement: Magyarosuchus possessed osteoderms arranged in two dorsal rows and at least two ventral rows along its body.
facts.quote: Many partial osteoderms and some complete ones are known, these would've been arranged in two dorsal, and at least two ventral rows along the body.

facts.statement: Dorsal osteoderms of Magyarosuchus were mostly square, overlapped the one behind them, and possessed a small lateral ridge.
facts.quote: Each dorsal osteoderm overlapped the one behind it, they were mostly square, and possessed a small lateral ridge.

facts.statement: Ventral osteoderms of Magyarosuchus overlapped front-to-back, were tightly sutured to neighbors, and were much wider than long.
facts.quote: The ventral osteoderms also overlapped front-to-back, and were tightly sutured to the ones beside them, these were much wider than long.

facts.statement: Magyarosuchus is classified as an early member of the clade Metriorhynchoidea.
facts.quote: Magyarosuchus is an early member of the clade Metriorhynchoidea.

facts.statement: Due to its large size and unique trait combination, Magyarosuchus represents a transitional form between fully marine metriorhynchids and their earlier non-marine ancestors.
facts.quote: Along its size (larger than any other non-metriorhynchid metriorhynchoid) this combination of traits show that Magyarosuchus represents a transitional form between the fully ocean going metriorhynchids and their earlier non-marine ancestors.

facts.statement: Magyarosuchus was found in the Kisgerecse Marl Formation, which indicates an open-ocean environment.
facts.quote: Magyarosuchus was discovered in the Kisgerecse Marl Formation, whose deposits indicate a more open-ocean environment.

facts.statement: Magyarosuchus represents the oldest known thalattosuchian adapted to open-ocean conditions rather than coastal or lagoonal habitats.
facts.quote: It represents the oldest known thalattosuchian adapted to such conditions, rather than to coastal or lagoonal habitats.

facts.statement: Magyarosuchus belongs to the suborder Thalattosuchia.
Magyarosuchus belongs to the superfamily Metriorhynchoidea.
